pathAssignments.学生内容:
A school wanted to reduce the number of disposable cups used during events. At first, leaders planned to ban the cups immediately. Students surveyed families and discovered that some visitors forgot to bring reusable bottles. The school changed its plan: it installed water refill points, sold low-cost reusable cups and kept a small supply of paper cups for emergencies. After two events, disposable-cup use fell by 72 percent. The result suggested that providing practical alternatives helped the policy work.

Which action was an alternative to disposable cups?

A. Cancelling the survey
B. Removing all water
C. Increasing ticket prices
D. Installing refill points
pathAssignments.解析: Refill points supported reusable containers.

Mangrove forests grow where land and sea meet. Their tangled roots slow moving water and trap mud, creating shelter for young fish and crabs. The roots also reduce the force of waves before those waves reach the shore. Yet mangroves are sometimes removed to make space for roads or buildings. In one coastal town, students helped map the remaining trees. Their map showed that places with thicker mangrove growth had lost less soil after storms. How do mangroves help young fish?

B. They remove all mud
C. They create sheltered areas
D. They make waves stronger
pathAssignments.解析: The roots create shelter for young fish and crabs.
